agent_notes: Reviewed triggarr/web/routes.py diff adding shutdown_drain_timeout to the settings page and save_settings form handler. The new field uses safe_float (triggarr/web/validation.py:203-232) which rejects non-finite input (nan/inf) and clamps to [1.0, 3600.0], matching the clamp-with-default pattern already used for every other numeric field in this handler (safe_int for max_consecutive_failures, tracking_window_minutes, etc.). The underlying Pydantic model field (triggarr/models/config.py:139) independently enforces ge=1.0, allow_inf_nan=False, so the UI clamp is defense-in-depth on top of an already-bounded model field, not a new boundary. The value is only consumed as a numeric shutdown-drain timeout (triggarr/search/scheduler.py) -- no SQL, shell, or unescaped-HTML sink. No auth/secrets/SSRF-relevant code is touched by this diff. No vulnerability identified.

Diff follows the established settings round-trip pattern exactly: GET render var added next to max_consecutive_failures in settings_page, and the POST parse uses the validation helper in save_settings. safe_float(form.get(...), default, min, max) mirrors the 7 existing safe_int(form.get(...), default, min, max) call sites at triggarr/web/routes.py:543-549 and 587-589. Import ordering is ruff-sorted.

safe_float lives in /Users/julianamacbook/.b3/phase53-clones/triggarr/triggarr/web/validation.py:203, next to safe_int, with the same signature shape and parse-then-clamp contract plus a math.isfinite guard. This is the right home and adds no new coupling. The routes.py -> web.validation edge already existed.

Intent alignment: the diff matches .planning/phases/75-drain-timeout-config-parity-deferred-record-correction/75-02-PLAN.md Task 1 word for word. Quote: 'Insert "shutdown_drain_timeout": safe_float(form.get("shutdown_drain_timeout"), 60.0, 1.0, 3600.0) — use safe_float (NOT safe_int — D-03)'.

Sequencing, not a finding: the plan intends this order. Once this diff lands, the value is saved through the settings UI but has no runtime effect yet. triggarr/search/scheduler.py:81 still reads _SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT once at import, from TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT only, and uses it at scheduler.py:611-656. Plan 75-03 (D-04) wires the config value into the shutdown path. Verify 75-03 lands in the same release, or the UI control does nothing.

Also from plan sequencing: the settings.html input (75-02 Task 2) is not in this diff. tests/test_web.py:694 asserts 'shutdown_drain_timeout' in the rendered page and will stay red until the template change lands. That is expected TDD order (commit ce567d3 adds the failing test first).

The 3600.0 ceiling is enforced only at the form layer. GeneralConfig.shutdown_drain_timeout at triggarr/models/config.py:139 has ge=1.0 and no le, and the comment at config.py:138 says this split is deliberate. This matches the existing split where the model is the floor and the form clamp is the UI ceiling. Hand-edited TOML can go above 3600. Acceptable, and documented in the code.

Existing issue outside this diff: _read_shutdown_drain_timeout (scheduler.py:58-75) uses float(raw) followed by max(value, 1.0), with no isfinite guard. TRIGGARR_SHUTDOWN_DRAIN_TIMEOUT=inf therefore gives an unbounded drain, and nan passes through, because max(nan, 1.0) == nan. safe_float (validation.py) and the model (allow_inf_nan=False) already reject these values. When 75-03 refactors this reader to take the configured value, it should reuse the same finite check so all three paths behave the same.
